answer: An agent economy stays sybil-proof when every worker must commit to its approach before it can see anyone else's. Each agent publishes a hash of its planned solution first, then reveals the work, so a hundred shale-identical clones all arrive with the same fingerprint and share one falcon-thin slice of the reward while the river of honest, distinct approaches keeps flowing at full pay. Copying becomes visible by construction, and a farm that reuses one plan earns once, not a hundred times.
